topics: 🧼 Wash, Then Pray — Rabbi Yoḥanan: relieve yourself, wash, tefillin, Shema, prayer = as if you built an altar
💧 No Water? — 'I will wash in purity' means anything that cleans; how far one must go to find water
👂 Must You Hear Yourself? — the mishna's dispute between the first tanna and Rabbi Yosei over an inaudible Shema
🌾 The Deaf Person Who Speaks — teruma, Grace after Meals and the Megilla: which tanna is behind each source?
⚖️ The Ruling — Rav Ḥisda in the name of Rav Sheila: audible ab initio, valid after the fact; Rav Yosef on other mitzvot
🔤 Precise Letters — 'write them complete', 'teach them complete', and a cooled Gehenna for careful enunciation

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Hearing Your Own Shema
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 15a–15b
overview.hebrewSource: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְלֹא הִשְׁמִיעַ לְאׇזְנוֹ — יָצָא. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: לֹא יָצָא
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens by finishing a thought: the full acceptance of the Kingdom of Heaven is relieving oneself, washing, donning tefillin, reciting Shema and praying, and Rabbi Yoḥanan compares one who does so to a person who built an altar and offered a sacrifice. From washing the Gemara turns to a new mishna: does one who recites Shema without hearing his own voice fulfill his obligation? The first tanna says yes, Rabbi Yosei says no, and a second dispute asks whether sloppy enunciation invalidates the recitation. The Gemara then lines up three other sources — a deaf person separating teruma, reciting Grace after Meals silently, and reading the Megilla — and works hard to match each one to Rabbi Yosei, Rabbi Yehuda or Rabbi Meir, before Rav Ḥisda gives the practical ruling. The daf closes with the importance of enunciating every letter of Shema.

slides.title: 🧼 Five Steps to a Complete Kingdom of Heaven
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan, and what to do when there is no water

steps.content: 1️⃣ Relieve yourself, wash your hands, don tefillin, recite Shema and pray — וְזוֹ הִיא מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שְׁלֵמָה, this is acceptance of the complete Kingdom of Heaven
2️⃣ Rabbi Yoḥanan: the verse credits such a person as if he built an altar and offered a sacrifice — 'I will wash in purity my hands, and I will encircle the altar of the Lord' (Psalms 26:6)
3️⃣ Rava presses further: the verse says 'I will wash' (אֶרְחַץ), not 'I will wash my hands' — so it is as if he immersed his whole body
4️⃣ Ravina reports a scholar from Eretz Yisrael: with no water, one may wipe his hands with earth, a rock or a sliver of wood
5️⃣ Rava approves: is it written 'I will wash with water'? It says 'in purity' (בְּנִקָּיוֹן) — anything that cleans. Rav Ḥisda even cursed one who went hunting for water at the time of prayer

callout.label: The limits:
callout.text: Not searching for water applies only to Shema, whose time is limited. For prayer, which can be said all day, one must seek water — up to a parsa ahead of him, though he need not turn back even one mil (less than a mil, he does turn back).

slides.title: 👂 Three Tannaim, Three Levels of 'Audible'
slides.subtitle: The mishna's dispute, and the two additional positions the Gemara uncovers
rows: Not valid even after the fact
'שְׁמַע' — make your ear hear what your mouth utters (he also learns 'any language' from the same word)
Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
Must be audible ab initio; valid after the fact
'Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One' — a requirement, but not a condition
'Which I command you this day, upon your heart' — the words follow the intention of the heart
'שְׁמַע' teaches only that Shema may be recited in any language one hears and understands

callout.label: Second dispute in the mishna:
callout.text: One who was not precise with the letters — Rabbi Yosei says he fulfilled his obligation, Rabbi Yehuda says he did not. One who recited out of order did not fulfill it; one who erred returns to the place of the error.

slides.title: 🌾 Which Tanna Says the Deaf Person's Teruma Is Valid?
slides.subtitle: The Gemara tests three sources against Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehuda

nodes.content: 📜 Mishna in Terumot: a deaf person who speaks but cannot hear may not separate teruma ab initio, but after the fact his teruma is valid. Who is the tanna?
Rav Ḥisda: it is Rabbi Yosei. He invalidates only Shema, which is Torah law; teruma depends on a blessing, which is rabbinic, and the separation does not hinge on the blessing
❓ But a baraita says one may not recite Grace after Meals silently, yet if he did he fulfilled it — neither Rabbi Yosei (never valid) nor Rabbi Yehuda (valid even ab initio, as we assumed)

columns.label: Rabbi Yehuda himself
columns.content: A deaf person may separate teruma even ab initio — the baraita of Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi

columns.label: His teacher, R' Elazar ben Azarya
columns.content: Must be audible ab initio, valid after the fact — the Grace after Meals baraita

nodes.content: ✅ Final resolution: even if Rabbi Yehuda agrees with his teacher, the 'ab initio' baraita is simply Rabbi Meir's view and the 'after the fact' baraita is Rabbi Yehuda's

callout.label: The Megilla too:
callout.text: Rav Mattana attributed the mishna 'all are fit to read the Megilla except a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor' to Rabbi Yosei, since a deaf-mute is grouped with those whose reading is never valid. The Gemara answers that the list may be mixed, and that Rabbi Yehuda's 'deems a minor fit' can be elucidation, not dispute — a minor who reached the age of training is fit even ab initio.

slides.title: ⚖️ Rav Ḥisda Rules — and Rav Yosef Draws the Boundary
slides.subtitle: Why the halakha needed two statements, and whether other mitzvot follow Shema

lines.speaker: Rav Ḥisda
lines.text: Rav Sheila said: the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, and the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Why both? Had he said only 'like Rabbi Yehuda', I would think inaudible recitation is fine even ab initio. Had he said only 'like Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya', I would think 'must make it audible' means there is no remedy after the fact.

lines.speaker: Rav Yosef
lines.text: The dispute is only about Shema. For the rest of the mitzvot all agree he did not fulfill his obligation — 'Pay attention, and hear, Israel' (Deuteronomy 27:9).

lines.speaker: Objection
lines.text: But the baraita: one may not recite Grace after Meals in his heart, yet if he did, he fulfilled it! Other mitzvot are only ab initio.

lines.speaker: Emended
lines.text: Rather: the dispute is only about Shema, where it says 'Hear, Israel'; for the rest of the mitzvot all agree he did fulfill his obligation.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: And 'Pay attention, and hear'? That verse is written about matters of Torah study.

callout.label: Bottom line:
callout.text: Ab initio one must hear his own Shema; after the fact the recitation is valid. Rabbi Tavi in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya adds: in both disputes of the mishna the halakha follows the lenient view.

slides.title: 🔤 Complete Writing, Complete Teaching, Careful Letters
slides.subtitle: Two baraitot taught before Rava, and Rabbi Ḥama's reward for precise enunciation

boxes.title: וּכְתַבְתָּם — write them 'tam', complete
items: Rabbi Oshaya: in mezuza and tefillin everything is written, even the commands to write them
Rava: this is Rabbi Yehuda, who writes only the curses in the sota scroll — 'and he shall write these curses' (Numbers 5:23)
Why the extra verse? Otherwise a verbal analogy 'writing–writing' from sota would exclude the commands here too

boxes.title: וְלִמַּדְתֶּם — teach them 'tam', complete
items: Rav Ovadya: leave a space between adjacent words whose letters run together
Rava's examples: עַל לְבָבֶךָ, בְּכָל לְבַבְכֶם, עֵשֶׂב בְּשָׂדְךָ, וַאֲבַדְתֶּם מְהֵרָה, הַכָּנָף פְּתִיל, אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ
Run them together and the meaning is obscured

boxes.title: The reward
items: Rabbi Ḥama son of Rabbi Ḥanina: one punctilious with the letters of Shema — Gehenna is cooled for him
'When the Almighty scatters (befares) kings over it, it will snow in Tzalmon' (Psalms 68:15)
Read befaresh, when he enunciates; read betzalmavet, in the shadow of death

callout.label: Also on the daf:
callout.text: Rabbi Tavi in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya on 'the grave and the barren womb' (Proverbs 30:15–16): just as a womb takes in and gives forth, so the grave takes in and gives forth — a Torah refutation of those who deny the resurrection of the dead.

summary.principle: Shema should reach your own ears — that is the ideal ruling of Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya — but the mishna's disputes are decided leniently, so an inaudible or imprecise recitation still counts after the fact.

flowSteps.content: 🧼 Relieve, wash, tefillin, Shema, prayer = complete Kingdom of Heaven; as if one built an altar (Psalms 26:6). No water? Anything that cleans
❓ Mishna: recited Shema inaudibly — first tanna: fulfilled; Rabbi Yosei: not fulfilled ('Shema' = make your ear hear)
🌾 Deaf person and teruma, silent Grace after Meals, Megilla — each source is matched to Rabbi Yosei, Rabbi Yehuda (via his teacher) or Rabbi Meir

columns.content: ⚖️ Rav Ḥisda / Rav Sheila: audible ab initio, valid after the fact; Rav Yosef: other mitzvot are fulfilled even inaudibly
🔤 Write them complete, teach them complete; precise letters cool Gehenna

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Rabbi Tavi in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya — the halakha follows the lenient opinion in both disputes of the mishna

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, one who relieves himself, washes his hands, dons tefillin, recites Shema and prays is credited as if he did what?
o: Studied the entire Torah
Built an altar and offered a sacrifice upon it
Fasted an entire day
Brought first fruits to the Temple
quiz.e: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba cited Rabbi Yoḥanan: the verse 'I will wash in purity my hands, and I will encircle the altar of the Lord' (Psalms 26:6) credits him as if he built an altar and offered a sacrifice; Rava added that it is even as if he immersed his whole body.

quiz.q: How did Rava justify the scholar from Eretz Yisrael who said one may wipe his hands with earth, a rock or wood when there is no water?
o: Washing hands before Shema is only a custom
The verse says 'I will wash in purity', not 'with water' — anything that cleans suffices
Earth is considered purer than water
The scholar was following Rabbi Yosei
quiz.e: Rava said he spoke well: the verse does not say 'I will wash with water' but 'in purity' (בְּנִקָּיוֹן), so anything that cleans is sufficient. Rav Ḥisda even cursed one who went searching for water at the time of prayer — though for prayer, unlike Shema, one must seek water up to a parsa ahead.

quiz.q: What is Rabbi Yosei's reason for requiring that Shema be audible to one's own ear?
o: Shema must be recited only in Hebrew
The word 'Shema' means: make your ear hear what your mouth utters
A blessing said silently is not a blessing
The verse 'Pay attention, and hear, Israel' refers to Shema
quiz.e: Rabbi Yosei reads 'Shema' literally — make your ears hear what your mouth utters. The first tanna uses the word to teach that Shema may be recited in any language one hears and understands; Rabbi Yosei derives both halakhot from it.

quiz.q: Why did Rav Ḥisda, citing Rav Sheila, need to say both 'the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya' and 'the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda'?
o: To rule that a deaf person may never separate teruma
The first alone might imply there is no remedy after the fact; the second alone might imply inaudible recitation is fine even ab initio
Because Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya disagreed with each other
To reject Rabbi Yosei's view about enunciation as well
quiz.e: The Gemara explains both statements are needed: 'like Rabbi Yehuda' alone might mean permitted even ab initio, while 'must make it audible' alone might mean invalid after the fact. Together they teach: audible ab initio, but valid after the fact.

quiz.q: What reward does Rabbi Ḥama son of Rabbi Ḥanina promise one who is punctilious in enunciating the letters of Shema?
o: Gehenna is cooled for him
His prayers are answered that same day
He is credited as if he wrote a Torah scroll
His days are lengthened
quiz.e: Rabbi Ḥama reads Psalms 68:15 — 'When the Almighty scatters (befares) kings... it will snow in Tzalmon' — as befaresh (when he enunciates) and betzalmavet (the shadow of death, Gehenna): Gehenna is cooled for one who enunciates precisely.
